description: Patterns for automatically detecting and validating data types, mixed types, suspicious columns, and inconsistent formatting

type_detection_rules.name: Numeric Masquerading as String
type_detection_rules.detection: Column dtype is 'object' BUT >80% of non-null values can be parsed as float/int
type_detection_rules.recommended_fix: Strip formatting characters → convert to float → handle unparseable as NaN
type_detection_rules.example: Column 'revenue' detected as string but 94% values are numeric with $ prefix. Stripped '$' and ',' → converted to float64. 6% unparseable values ('N/A', '-') treated as missing.

type_detection_rules.name: Date Masquerading as String
type_detection_rules.detection: Column dtype is 'object' AND >60% values match common date patterns (MM/DD/YYYY, YYYY-MM-DD, DD-Mon-YY, etc.)
type_detection_rules.recommended_fix: Identify dominant format → pd.to_datetime with format parameter → decompose into features
type_detection_rules.example: Column 'order_date' contains dates in 3 different formats (MM/DD/YYYY: 67%, DD/MM/YYYY: 28%, YYYY-MM-DD: 5%). Standardized to YYYY-MM-DD. ⚠️ 28% had DD/MM/YYYY — ambiguous dates like '03/04/2024' may be misinterpreted.

type_detection_rules.name: Mixed Date Formats
type_detection_rules.detection: Date column has multiple formats or timezone inconsistencies
type_detection_rules.impact: Dates like '03/04/2024' are ambiguous — March 4th or April 3rd depending on locale. Wrong interpretation corrupts time-series analysis.
type_detection_rules.recommended_fix: Identify locale context from other data → apply consistent parsing → flag ambiguous dates for review
type_detection_rules.example: ⚠️ 'transaction_date' has ambiguous dates: 847 records where day/month could be swapped. Dates like '05/06/2024' are unparseable without locale context. Flagged for human review.

type_detection_rules.name: Boolean Masquerading as String
type_detection_rules.detection: Column has ≤5 unique values AND values match boolean patterns
type_detection_rules.recommended_fix: Map to boolean/binary (0/1) for ML readiness
type_detection_rules.example: Column 'is_active' contains ['Yes', 'No', 'yes', 'YES', 'N/A']. Standardized case → mapped Yes=1, No=0, N/A=NaN.

type_detection_rules.name: ID Column Detection
type_detection_rules.detection: Column has unique values ≈ row count AND/OR name matches ID patterns
type_detection_rules.recommended_action: Exclude from ML features. Keep as reference/join key only.
type_detection_rules.example: Column 'emp_code' identified as ID column (100% unique, sequential pattern). Excluded from feature set — IDs have no predictive power and cause overfitting.

suspicious_column_patterns.name: Constant Column
suspicious_column_patterns.detection: Column has only 1 unique value across all rows
suspicious_column_patterns.action: Drop — zero variance provides no information
suspicious_column_patterns.example: Column 'country' has value 'India' in all 5,000 rows. Dropped — provides no analytical value.

suspicious_column_patterns.name: Near-Constant Column
suspicious_column_patterns.detection: Column has 1 dominant value appearing in >98% of rows
suspicious_column_patterns.action: Review — the rare values may be interesting anomalies or data errors
suspicious_column_patterns.example: Column 'currency' is 'INR' for 99.2% of records. The 0.8% 'USD' entries may be legitimate international transactions or data entry errors.

suspicious_column_patterns.name: All-Unique Column (Possible Free Text or ID)
suspicious_column_patterns.detection: Column has unique values equal to row count AND is not detected as ID
suspicious_column_patterns.action: Investigate — may be free text (addresses, comments) that needs NLP or should be dropped for ML
suspicious_column_patterns.example: Column 'comments' has 5,000 unique values across 5,000 rows. This appears to be free-text data — exclude from ML features unless NLP feature extraction is applied.

suspicious_column_patterns.name: Column with Embedded Delimiters
suspicious_column_patterns.detection: String column where >20% of values contain commas, pipes, or semicolons
suspicious_column_patterns.action: This column may contain multiple values packed into one field. Consider splitting into separate columns.
suspicious_column_patterns.example: Column 'tags' contains values like 'electronics,sale,featured'. Split into 3 boolean columns: 'tag_electronics', 'tag_sale', 'tag_featured'.

suspicious_column_patterns.name: Suspiciously Correlated with Index
suspicious_column_patterns.detection: Numeric column has correlation >0.95 with row index
suspicious_column_patterns.action: This column may be a sequential ID or auto-generated field masquerading as a feature. Verify business meaning.
suspicious_column_patterns.example: Column 'serial_no' has 0.99 correlation with row index. This is an auto-generated sequence, not a meaningful feature. Excluded from analysis.

inconsistent_formatting_patterns.name: Inconsistent Case
inconsistent_formatting_patterns.detection: String column has values that differ only in capitalization
inconsistent_formatting_patterns.fix: Apply consistent casing (title case for names, lowercase for codes)
inconsistent_formatting_patterns.impact: Creates phantom categories in groupby operations

inconsistent_formatting_patterns.name: Leading/Trailing Whitespace
inconsistent_formatting_patterns.detection: String values have spaces before or after actual content
inconsistent_formatting_patterns.impact: Invisible to users but causes failed joins and phantom categories

inconsistent_formatting_patterns.name: Inconsistent Null Representations
inconsistent_formatting_patterns.detection: Column contains multiple different null/missing representations
inconsistent_formatting_patterns.fix: Map all variants to proper NaN. CRITICAL: '0' and '-1' may be legitimate values — verify with domain context.
inconsistent_formatting_patterns.impact: These remain invisible to pandas isnull() — they appear as valid data but are actually missing.

inconsistent_formatting_patterns.name: Mixed Number Formats
inconsistent_formatting_patterns.detection: Numeric column contains values with different decimal/thousand separators
inconsistent_formatting_patterns.fix: Detect dominant format → standardize → convert to float
inconsistent_formatting_patterns.impact: Mixing formats causes values to be misinterpreted by 100x-1000x

inconsistent_formatting_patterns.name: Encoding Issues (Mojibake)
inconsistent_formatting_patterns.detection: String column contains garbled characters (Ã¢, â€™, Ã©, etc.)
inconsistent_formatting_patterns.fix: Re-read file with correct encoding (UTF-8, Latin-1, cp1252). Try ftfy library for automatic fix.
inconsistent_formatting_patterns.impact: Customer names, addresses, and product names become unreadable

cardinality_analysis.description: Rules for analyzing and acting on column cardinality

high.action: Target encode with regularization, or embeddings

very_high.action: Hash encoding, or drop if not predictive. Consider if this is actually an ID column.
